# Configuration

<!-- Generated from crates/vtium/src/config/keys.rs; do not edit. `VTIUM_BLESS=1 cargo test -p vtium generated_files` rewrites it. -->

vtium reads `vtium.conf` in the configuration directory (`--configdir`, `/etc/vtium` by default), then `<seat>.seat.conf` there, then its command line. Each wins over the ones before it. vtium never reads the C reference's `/etc/kmscon`: a `kmscon.conf` from kmscon is copied to `/etc/vtium/vtium.conf` by hand, and vtium reads its keys as the C reference did, with the departures the vtium crate's README lists. A file that does not exist is skipped. The files are read once, at start: a change applies when vtium starts again, as at a restart of its service. `vtium check-config [FILE]` reads them as the start would, with the head file, `/etc/vtium/heads.conf`, or FILE in its place to check it before it is installed, through the start's parser and evaluator (ADR-1401 D7). It applies nothing, exits 1 on any warning and on each of the head file's errors and warnings, each named with its line, and notes on standard output what it does not count: the density points convert at, and of the head file each rule sending input to a head by `id` or `name` alone, where no udev daemon runs, each rule using a key that reads udev's database, each rule using `connector-path:`, which it cannot check against the displays present since it opens no card to read a connector's `PATH`, a head no rule names, every head isolated, and what the devices present find: each rule matching none of them, each device no rule places with what the policy gives it, no head that can be the active head having a display, under a closed policy no keyboard reaching any head, a head claiming pointers while every keyboard is claimed elsewhere, every keyboard ignored, and a head whose only keyboard is one device (ADR-1401 D9). It reads the devices from sysfs and udev's database, `/run/udev/data`, and opens nothing under `/dev`. A FILE that root does not own, or that others can write, is checked all the same, with a note, since installing it makes it root's.

A file holds one key a line: `key=value`, or a switch's `key` to turn it on and `no-key` to turn it off. `#` starts a comment, except where it opens a `#rrggbb` color value. Spaces and tabs around the key and the value are dropped. On the command line a key is `--key=VALUE` or `--key VALUE`, and a switch `--key` or `--no-key`.

vtium reports, once at start, a key it does not know, however often it appears, and a value it cannot use: a number out of bounds, which it clamps, and a value it cannot read, which it ignores, keeping the value the sources before it gave. It reads at most 65536 bytes of a file and 8192 of a line.

`install/vtium.conf.example` in `crates/vtium` lists the same keys at their defaults. Source cites the C reference, kmscon at `b1f7a7c5` ([c-reference.md](c-reference.md)), or the decision a key comes from.

## Other color schemes for the notices and the on-screen display

`install/vtium.conf.example` carries these schemes for the six color keys, commented out, for color blindness and personal preference (ADR-1401 D5). vtium draws whatever colors are set and checks no contrast between a text and its box.

| Scheme | What it is | `notice-foreground` | `notice-background` | `notice-border` | `osd-foreground` | `osd-background` | `osd-border` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `light` | For a light terminal background: the on-screen display is a pale grey box with dark text and a grey edge, and a notice a dark red box with white text and a darker edge, so a problem differs from a status in brightness as well as in hue. | `255,255,255` | `153,27,27` | `69,10,10` | `31,41,51` | `243,244,246` | `156,163,175` |
| `dark` | Both boxes are dark, for a dark terminal background: a notice is deep red with pale text and a light red edge, and the on-screen display near black with light grey text and a grey edge. | `254,226,226` | `185,28,28` | `248,113,113` | `209,213,219` | `17,24,39` | `75,85,99` |
| `color-blind-safe` | For color blindness, a problem differs from a status in brightness and in an orange and blue pair, never in red against green: a notice is a bright orange box with near-black text, and the on-screen display a dark blue box with near-white text. | `28,25,23` | `255,176,0` | `254,97,0` | `238,242,255` | `11,42,91` | `100,143,255` |
